problem:
Given that

$$
\frac{7x}{({x}^{2}+3)(x-2)}=\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+3}+\frac{C}{x-2},
$$

where $A,$ $B$ and $C$ are real constants, determine the value of $A+B+C.$

feedback.worked_solution:
Our task is to find $A$, $B$, and $C$ such that

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{({x}^{2}+4)(x+2)}=\frac{Ax+B}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{C}{x+2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Multiplying both sides by $({x}^{2}+4)(x+2)$ gives

$$
5=(Ax+B)(x+2)+C({x}^{2}+4).
$$

For $x=-2$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =C(4+4) \\ 5 & =8C \\ C & =\frac{5}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x=0$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =(A(0)+B)(0+2)+\frac{5}{8}((0)^{2}+4) \\ 5 & =2B+\frac{5}{2} \\ 2B & =\frac{5}{2} \\ B & =\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

For $x=1$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}5 & =(A(1)+\frac{5}{4})(1+2)+\frac{5}{8}((1)^{2}+4) \\ 5 & =3A+\frac{15}{4}+\frac{25}{8} \\ 3A & =-\frac{15}{8} \\ A & =-\frac{5}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{5}{({x}^{2}+4)(x+2)} & =\frac{(-\frac{5}{8}x+\frac{5}{4})}{{x}^{2}+4}+\frac{(\frac{5}{8})}{x+2} \\  & =\frac{-5\,x+10}{8({x}^{2}+4)}+\frac{5}{8(x+2)}\end{aligned}
$$
